subject.title: exec private-LAN access fails while same user GUI/LaunchAgent succeeds

question: Should this issue be resolved by a diagnostic-only exec warning, or should OpenClaw change private-LAN reachability semantics for gateway-host exec?
rationale: Source inspection can show the missing diagnostic, but allowing, blocking, or detaching private-LAN exec traffic changes the operator-controlled shell/network security boundary and needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Land Diagnostic Only
options.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR while leaving actual private-LAN access policy unchanged and tracked by the related security issues.

options.title: Design Access Parity
options.body: Treat same-user GUI/LaunchAgent reachability parity as the product goal and require a separate security design before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Broader Trackers
options.body: Reject the diagnostic-only scope and handle this only through the broader private-network policy trackers.

recommendation.title: Land Diagnostic Only
recommendation.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR while leaving actual private-LAN access policy unchanged and tracked by the related security issues.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans exec UX, macOS gateway behavior, and security-default policy where Peter's recent exec/docs history is the strongest routing signal.
